title: Bootstrap entropy/init failure fingerprints — TF probe plan and smoke checklist
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a narrow but recurring class of private-deploy failures we see during bootstrap and early runtime init: low entropy / RNG stalls, intermittent GPU driver init errors, early network mount timeouts (PXE/iSCSI/NFS), and terraform race conditions that manifest as flakey resource attachments. The goal is a short fingerprint checklist (quick probes + log regexes) + a small TF probe plan / idempotent re-run flow operators can use before rolling back or escalating to SRE.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Private (VPC and on-prem) installs where we run terraform modules to provision nodes and then a runtime install (systemd units, containers, driver modules).
- Assumes SSH access to bootstrap host(s) and kube control-plane where applicable.
- Not a full playbook; this is a focused troubleshooting primer to speed TTR for the specific failure signatures.

Quick symptom-to-probe map (2–8 min triage):
1) Symptom: long TLS/HTTPS handshake timeouts during install (applies early, before services up).
   Probe: ssh into node; run:
     sudo dd if=/dev/random bs=1 count=64 2>/dev/null | hexdump -C
   Expected (healthy): returns immediately.
   Fingerprint (entropy-starved): command hangs for >3s or returns very slowly.
   Why: initramfs/VM/images without enough entropy block on /dev/random. Causes delays when getting certs or talking to KMS/HSM.
   Mitigation (fast):
     - install haveged or rng-tools in image; for immediate workaround: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y haveged && sudo systemctl start haveged
     - For air-gapped installs, seed /dev/random with: sudo dd if=/dev/urandom of=/dev/random bs=64 count=4

2) Symptom: runtime processes crash with TLS failure logs referencing "PRNG" or "failed to initialize secure RNG".
   Probes: grep -E "entropy|PRNG|random|RNG|failed to initialize" /var/log/* -R | head -n 40
   Fingerprints: repeated lines around service startup with timestamps clustered at boot.

3) Symptom: GPU driver modules fail to bind or large OOM during init of runtime containers.
   Probes:
     - sudo dmesg | grep -i -E "nvidia|amdgpu|gpu|vfio|iommu" | tail -n 60
     - lsmod | egrep "nvidia|nvidia_drm|amdgpu"
     - sudo systemctl status nvidia-persistenced || true
   Fingerprint signatures:
     - dmesg: "NVRM: Xid (GPU has fallen off the bus)" => hardware PCI errors / cabling / BIOS settings
     - dmesg: "Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch" => driver/runtime mismatch (kernel module vs container toolkit)
   Quick mitigations:
     - ensure host kernel headers match installed driver package; for Ubuntu: sudo apt-get install --reinstall linux-headers-$(uname -r) nvidia-driver-XXX
     - restart container runtime and gpu-device-plugin: sudo systemctl restart containerd && kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/gpu-device-plugin

4) Symptom: storage mounts (iSCSI/NFS) time out during preflight or container pull.
   Probes:
     - sudo systemctl status iscsid || true; sudo iscsiadm -m session -P3
     - show mounts: mount | grep -E "iscsi|nfs"
   Fingerprint: repeated kernel timeouts in dmesg containing "NFS server not responding" or "iSCSI: Login to target.*failed"
   Quick mitigation:
     - verify MTU mismatches across vNICs; sudo ip link show && sudo ethtool -k <iface> to check.
     - re-provision route/peer via control plane and retry iscsiadm discovery

Terraform-specific flaky patterns and probe plan:
- Pattern A: "resource already exists" when provider retries run concurrently across modules (race on attach).
  Probe: run terraform plan -target=<suspect_resource> to confirm state drift.
  Quick TF commands:
    terraform init -input=false
    terraform plan -refresh=true -input=false -out=tfplan
  Detection regex in CLI output: "Error:.*already exists|conflict|resource is in use"
  Operator flow (idempotent attempt):
    1) terraform apply -target=<resource> -auto-approve -> if fails with "already exists" then run terraform state rm <resource> and re-import or use terraform import <resource> <id> (careful; escalate if unsure).
    2) If attach resources (ENIs, Volumes) intermittently fail, wait 30–90s and reapply once; collect terraform logs: TF_LOG=DEBUG terraform apply...

- Pattern B: provider-side 409/429 transient errors (API rate limits) during large-scale boots.
  Probe: check provider console (cloud audit) and any provider error messages in terraform state.
  Mitigation: stagger node creation with a small sleep in bootstrap orchestration or use resource 'create_before_destroy' toggles conservatively.

Log fingerprints (regexes to search quickly):
- Entropy / RNG: "(entropy|PRNG|random).*failed|blocking on /dev/random"
- Driver mismatch: "(Driver/library version mismatch|NVML|NVRM|GPU has fallen off the bus)"
- iSCSI/NFS: "(NFS server not responding|iSCSI: Login|iscsiadm: login failed)"
- Terraform race: "(already exists|resource is in use|conflict|Error: 409|Error: 429)"

Minimal smoke checklist (to run in order):
1) Node basic health (30–60s)
   - ssh <node>
   - uptime; free -m; df -h
   - sudo systemctl list-units --failed | sed -n '1,40p'

2) Entropy quick test (10s)
   - sudo dd if=/dev/random bs=1 count=64 2>/dev/null | hexdump -C || true
   - If >2s: check haveged/rng-tools status: sudo systemctl status haveged || sudo systemctl start haveged

3) Network probe (30s)
   - ping -c3 <api-endpoint> and curl -v https://<api-endpoint>/health
   - ip route show; sudo ethtool <iface> to check autoneg/tx-offload settings

4) Storage and mounts (30–90s)
   - mount | grep -E "nfs|iscsi"; sudo iscsiadm -m node || true; dmesg | tail -n 80 | egrep "NFS|iSCSI|iscsiadm"

5) GPU/runtime checks (30–90s)
   - lsmod | egrep "nvidia|amdgpu"; dmesg | egrep "NVML|NVRM|gpu" | tail -n 60
   - docker/ctr logs of runtime-manager service (kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=runtime-manager --tail=200)

6) Terraform quick sanity (2–5 min)
   - terraform init
   - terraform plan -refresh=true -target=<node_resource> -no-color | tee /tmp/tf-plan.out
   - grep -E "already exists|Error:|conflict|429|409" /tmp/tf-plan.out || true

Escalation hints (what to collect before paging SRE):
- node hostname, instance-id, boot timestamps (journalctl --since "-15m"), full dmesg output, /var/log/syslog and runtime manager logs, the exact terraform plan output with TF_LOG=DEBUG, and a list of recently created cloud resources (ENI/Volume ids).
- If GPU errors, capture: sudo nvidia-smi -a (or amd equivalent) and lsmod output.

Operator-friendly idempotent re-run pattern (safe steps):
1) Try non-destructive restarts: sudo systemctl restart network.service; sudo systemctl restart containerd
2) If entropy-starved: start haveged
3) If storage attach failure: unmount stale mounts, iscsiadm logout, then re-run iscsiadm discovery+login
4) If terraform show drift or partial apply: run terraform plan -target to reconcile. Avoid blanket terraform destroy unless necessary.

Notes from past incidents (fingerprint anecdotes):
- Incident PRIV-2024-11: had repeated bootstrap hangs while fetching certs; root cause: image created in CI lacked haveged and was booted in tiny VM pool, visible as entropy-starved pattern. Fix: added haveged to golden image and preseeded entropy in image build.
- Incident PRIV-2025-02: frequent GPU "driver mismatch" after upgrading node kernel via unattended apt; kernel headers mismatched driver package. Fix: pin driver package and add post-upgrade verify script to runtime install.

Appendix: Useful commands & canned regexes for quick copy
- Entropy test: sudo timeout 3s dd if=/dev/random bs=1 count=64 2>/dev/null | hexdump -C || echo "entropy-stall"
- Log grep: sudo journalctl -u runtime-manager --no-pager | egrep -i "entropy|PRNG|NVML|NVRM|iSCSI|NFS|already exists|resource is in use|429|409" | tail -n 200
- TF debug apply: export TF_LOG=DEBUG; terraform apply -auto-approve | tee /tmp/tf-debug.log
- Sample terraform re-import flow (example):
    terraform state list | grep aws_ebs_volume
    terraform import aws_ebs_volume.data_vol vol-0123456789abcdef

Outstanding follow-ups (TODO):
- Add automated entropy probe in bootstrap healthcheck (PR queued) -> github PR #212 (linked).
- Add kernel/driver verify step in post-upgrade gating policy for private clusters.
- Create a small diagnostic agent (single binary) that can be scp'd to node and run the above probes and output a single JSON report for SRE ingestion.

If you use this note, add a short incident marker to the confluence page linked above with quick copy of logs and which fingerprint matched.

Author note: this is intentionally terse — meant to be copy-pasted into an incident slack or a runbook checklist. If it proves useful, we'll expand into a step-by-step playbook and add to the main install runbook.
